title.zh: 卷一百八十二 列傳第六十九: 張起巖 歐陽玄 許有壬 宋本 謝端
title.en: Volume 182 Biographies 69: Zhang Qiyan, Ōuyang Xuan, Xu Youren, Song Ben, Xie Duan
title.raw: 卷一百八十二 列傳第六十九: 張起巖 歐陽玄 許有壬 宋本 謝端 Volume 182 Biographies 69: Zhang Qiyan, Ōuyang Xuan, Xu Youren, Song Ben, Xie Duan

sentences.zh: 張起岩

translations.literal: Zhang Qiyan
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qiyan

sentences.zh: 張起岩，字夢臣。

translations.literal: Zhang Qiyan, styled Mengchen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qiyan, whose style name was Mengchen.

sentences.zh: 其先章丘人，五季避地禹城。

translations.literal: His ancestors were people of Zhangqiu; during the Five Dynasties they fled to Yucheng.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears were from Zhangqiu; in the Five Dynasties period the family took refuge in Yucheng.

sentences.zh: 高祖迪，以元帥右監軍權濟南府事，徙家濟南。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Di, as Right Supervisor of the Marshalate, held acting authority over Jinan prefectural affairs and moved the family to Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Di served as right supervisor of the marshalate with acting charge of Jinan prefecture and resettled the family there.

sentences.zh: 當金之季，張榮據有章丘、鄒平、濟陽、長山、辛市、蒲台、新城、淄州之地，歲丙戌，歸於太祖，始終能效忠節，迪與其子福，實先後羽翼之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jin, Zhang Rong held Zhangqiu, Zouping, Jiyang, Changshan, Xinshi, Putai, Xincheng, and Zizhou; in the year bingxu he submitted to Taizu and remained loyal to the end. Di and his son Fu in fact supported him first and afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Jin, Zhang Rong controlled Zhangqiu, Zouping, Jiyang, Changshan, Xinshi, Putai, Xincheng, and Zizhou; in the bingxu year he submitted to Taizu and proved loyal to the end. Di and his son Fu were among those who aided him from the first.

sentences.zh: 福仕為濟南路軍民鎮撫兵鈐轄，權府事，生東昌錄事判官鐸，鐸生四川行省儒學副提舉範，範生起岩。

translations.literal: Fu served as Military and Civil Pacification Commissioner and Military Controller of Jinan Circuit, held acting prefectural authority, and fathered Duo, Recorder and Judge of Dongchang; Duo fathered Fan, Associate Commissioner of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat for Confucian Learning; Fan fathered Qiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was Jinan circuit military and civil pacification commissioner and military controller with acting prefectural duties; his son Duo became recorder and judge at Dongchang, whose son Fan was associate commissioner for Confucian learning on the Sichuan branch secretariat; Fan was Qiyan's father.

sentences.zh: 初，其母丘氏有娠，見長蛇數丈入榻下，已忽不見，乃驚而誕起岩。

translations.literal: Earlier, when his mother Lady Qiu was pregnant, she saw a serpent several zhang long enter beneath the couch; it then suddenly vanished, and in alarm she gave birth to Qiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Before his birth, his mother Lady Qiu, while pregnant, saw a serpent many zhang long slip under the couch and vanish; startled, she then bore Qiyan.

sentences.zh: 幼從其父學，年弱冠，以察舉為福山縣學教諭，值縣官捕蝗，移攝縣事。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under his father; at the weak-crown year he was nominated by investigation as instructor at Fushan County school. When the county magistrate went to catch locusts, he was transferred to act as county administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He studied with his father as a boy; at twenty he was nominated as instructor at the Fushan county school. When the magistrate went out to catch locusts, Qiyan was left to administer the county.

sentences.zh: 久之，聽斷明允，其民相率曰：「若得張教諭為真縣尹，吾屬何患焉。

translations.literal: After a long time his hearings were clear and fair, and the people together said: "If we could have Instructor Zhang as the real county magistrate, what would we have to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: Before long his judgments were clear and fair, and the people said among themselves, "If Instructor Zhang were our real magistrate, we would have nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 」政成，遷安丘。

translations.literal: " When his administration was complete, he was transferred to Anqiu.
translations.idiomatic: " When he had finished his term, he was moved to Anqiu.

sentences.zh: 中延祐乙卯進士，首選，除同知登州事，特旨改集賢修撰，轉國子博士，升國子監丞，進翰林待制，兼國史院編修官。

translations.literal: In the yimao year of the Yanyou reign he passed the jinshi examination as top choice, was appointed Associate Administrator of Dengzhou, then by special edict made Academician Compiler at the Hall of Gathered Talents, turned National University Erudite, rose to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, advanced to Hanlin Attendant Draftsman, and concurrently Compiler at the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in Yanyou's yimao year as first in the class, became associate administrator of Dengzhou, then by special order was made compiler at the Hall of Gathered Talents, erudite of the National University, vice director of the directorate of education, Hanlin attendant draftsman, and concurrent historiography compiler.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，服除，選為監察御史。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother; when mourning ended he was selected as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he was chosen investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 中書參政楊廷玉以墨敗，台臣奉旨就廟堂逮之下吏。

translations.literal: Central Secretariat Administrator Yang Tingyu was ruined by bribery; censors by imperial order arrested him in the hall of government and sent him down to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tingyu, a central secretariat administrator, fell for corruption; the censorate, by imperial order, seized him in the council hall and handed him to the judicial officers.

sentences.zh: 丞相倒剌沙疾其摧辱同列，悉誣台臣罔上，欲置之重辟。

translations.literal: Chancellor Toghto resented their humiliation of colleagues, wholly slandered the censors for deceiving the throne, and wished to impose heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Toghto hated their humiliation of fellow officials, accused the whole censorate of deceiving the throne, and sought to punish them severely.

sentences.zh: 起岩以新除留台，抗章論曰：「台臣按劾百官，論列朝政，職使然也。

translations.literal: Qiyan, newly appointed and remaining at the censorate, submitted a memorial arguing: "Censors investigate and impeach the hundred officials and discuss court government—it is the nature of their duty.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyan, newly appointed and still at the censorate, memorialized: "Censors investigate officials and discuss court affairs—that is their office.

sentences.zh: 今以奉職獲戾，風紀解體，正直結舌，忠良寒心，殊非盛世事。

translations.literal: Now that they are punished for doing their duty, discipline collapses, the upright are silenced, and the loyal are chilled—this is hardly a matter for a flourishing age.
translations.idiomatic: To punish them for performing it destroys discipline, silences the upright, and chills the loyal—hardly what a flourishing age should see.

sentences.zh: 且世皇建臺閣，廣言路，維持治體，陛下即位詔旨，動法祖宗。

translations.literal: Moreover Shizu established the censorate and broadened the path of remonstrance to sustain the body of government; Your Majesty's accession edicts constantly follow the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Kublai founded the censorate and widened free speech to uphold government; Your Majesty's accession edicts constantly follow the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 今台臣坐譴，公論杜塞，何謂法祖宗耶！

translations.literal: Now the censors sit in reproof and public opinion is blocked—what does it mean to follow the ancestors!"
translations.idiomatic: Now the censors are punished and public debate is stifled—how is that following the ancestors?"

sentences.zh: 」章三上，不報。

translations.literal: " He submitted the memorial three times without response.
translations.idiomatic: " He submitted it three times without answer.

sentences.zh: 起岩廷爭愈急，帝感悟，事乃得釋，猶皆坐罷免還鄉里。

translations.literal: Qiyan argued ever more urgently in court; the emperor was moved, the affair was released, yet all still sat in dismissal and returned to their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyan pressed his case in court; the emperor relented and the matter was dropped, though all were still dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 遷中書右司員外郎，進左司郎中，兼經筵官，拜太子右贊善。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Section Vice Director of the Central Secretariat, advanced to Left Section Director, concurrently Lecturer at the Classics Mat, and appointed Right Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He became right-section vice director of the central secretariat, then left-section director, classics mat lecturer, and right tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 丁外艱，服除，改燕王府司馬，拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He mourned his father; when mourning ended he was changed to Prince of Yan's Chief of Staff and appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he was made chief of staff to the Prince of Yan and minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 文宗親郊，起岩充大禮使，導帝陟降，步武有節，衣前後襜如，陪位百官，望之如古圖畫中所睹。

translations.literal: When Wenzong personally performed the suburban sacrifice, Qiyan served as Grand Master of Rites, guiding the emperor up and down; his steps had measure, his robes before and behind hung evenly, and the officials in attendance looking at him seemed to see figures from ancient paintings.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong sacrificed at the suburbs, Qiyan was grand master of rites, guiding the emperor's ascent and descent with measured steps and even hanging robes; officials in attendance thought him a figure stepped from an old painting.

sentences.zh: 帝甚嘉之，賜賚優渥。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly praised him and bestowed rich rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him highly and gave him generous gifts.

sentences.zh: 轉參議中書省事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Secretariat Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made secretariat counselor.

sentences.zh: 寧宗崩，燕南俄起大獄，有妄男子上變，言部使者謀不軌，按問皆虛，法司謂：「《唐律》，告叛者不反坐。

translations.literal: When Ningzong died, Yan South soon saw a great case: a reckless man submitted a report saying a branch commissioner plotted sedition; investigation proved it all false, and the law officers said: "In the Tang Code, one who reports rebellion is not punished in return."
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ningzong's death a great case erupted in Yan South: a madman reported that a branch commissioner plotted treason; inquiry found it false, and the law officers cited the Tang Code: informers on rebellion are not punished in return.

sentences.zh: 」起岩奮謂同列曰：「方今嗣君未立，人情危疑，不亟誅此人，以杜奸謀，慮妨大計。

translations.literal: " Qiyan spoke forcefully to his colleagues: "Now the heir is not yet established and the people are uneasy; if we do not quickly execute this man to cut off wicked plots, we fear harm to the great plan."
translations.idiomatic: " Qiyan urged his colleagues: "The heir is not yet enthroned and minds are uneasy; unless we execute this man at once to stop conspiracy, the great design may suffer."

sentences.zh: 」趣有司具獄，都人肅然，大事尋定。

translations.literal: " He urged the officials to complete the case; the capital grew solemn and the great affair was soon settled.
translations.idiomatic: " He pressed for a completed verdict; the capital grew quiet and the crisis passed.

sentences.zh: 中書方列坐銓選，起岩荐一士可用，丞相不悅，起岩即攝衣而起，丞相以為忤己。

translations.literal: The Secretariat was just sitting in a row for selection and appointment; Qiyan recommended a scholar as usable; the chancellor was displeased and Qiyan at once gathered his robes and rose; the chancellor thought him insubordinate.
translations.idiomatic: During a secretariat session on appointments Qiyan recommended a capable man; the chancellor took offense and Qiyan rose and left; the chancellor deemed it defiance.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林侍講學士、知制誥兼修國史，修三朝實錄，加同知經筵事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Academician Expositor, Draftsman, and Compiler of the National History, compiled the Veritable Records of three reigns, and was added as Associate Lecturer at the Classics Mat.
translations.idiomatic: He became Hanlin expositor, draftsman, and national history compiler, edited the veritable records of three reigns, and was made associate classics mat lecturer.

sentences.zh: 御史臺奏除浙西廉訪使，不允。

translations.literal: The Censorate memorialized appointing him Surveillance Commissioner of Western Zhe, which was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate proposed him surveillance commissioner of Western Zhe, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 已而擢陝西行台侍御史。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Attending Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to attending censor on the Shaanxi branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 將行，复留為侍講學士。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, he was again retained as Academician Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: About to leave, he was kept on again as expositor.

sentences.zh: 拜江南行台侍御史，召入中台，為侍御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attending Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat, summoned into the central censorate, and made Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made attending censor on the Jiangnan branch, summoned to the central censorate, and confirmed as attending censor.

sentences.zh: 轉燕南廉訪使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Surveillance Commissioner of Yan South.
translations.idiomatic: He became surveillance commissioner of Yan South.

sentences.zh: 搏擊豪強，不少容貸，貧民賴以吐氣。

translations.literal: He struck at the powerful without leniency, and the poor relied on him to breathe freely.
translations.idiomatic: He prosecuted the powerful without mercy, and the poor at last had voice.

sentences.zh: 滹沱河水為真定害，起岩論封河神為侯爵，而移文責之，復修其提防，瀹其湮鬱，水患遂息。

translations.literal: The Hutuo River harmed Zhending; Qiyan argued against enfeoffing the river god as marquis, sent a document reproving it, restored the dikes, dredged the choked channels, and the flood trouble ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The Hutuo flooded Zhending; Qiyan opposed ennobling the river god as marquis, sent a rebuking dispatch, repaired the dikes and dredged the silt, and the floods ceased.

sentences.zh: 升江南行台御史中丞，拜翰林學士承旨、知制誥兼修國史、知經筵事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat, appointed Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts, Draftsman, Compiler of the National History, and Lecturer at the Classics Mat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice censor-in-chief on the Jiangnan branch, Hanlin recipient of edicts, draftsman, national history compiler, and classics mat lecturer.

sentences.zh: 右丞相別裡怯不花為台臣所糾，去位。

translations.literal: Right Chancellor Bayan Qubilad was impeached by the censors and left office.
translations.idiomatic: Right chancellor Bayan Qubilad was impeached by the censors and left office.

sentences.zh: 未幾再入相，諷詞臣言台章之非，起岩執不可，聞者壯之。

translations.literal: Before long he entered the chancellery again and hinted to the drafting officials that the censorial memorial was wrong; Qiyan held firm and would not agree—hearers admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned as chancellor and urged the draftsmen to say the censorial charge was wrong; Qiyan refused—listeners admired his stand.

sentences.zh: 俄拜御史中丞，論事剴直，無所顧忌，與上官多不合。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief; in discussing affairs he was sharp and direct, without regard, and often at odds with superiors.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice censor-in-chief, spoke sharply and without fear, and often clashed with superiors.

sentences.zh: 詔修遼、金、宋三史，復命入翰林為承旨，充總裁官，積階至榮祿大夫。

translations.literal: An edict ordered compilation of the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song; he was again ordered into the Hanlin as Recipient of Edicts, made Chief Compiler, and accumulated rank to Grand Master for Glorious Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to compile the Liao, Jin, and Song histories, he re-entered the Hanlin as recipient of edicts and chief compiler, rising to grand master for glorious happiness.

sentences.zh: 起岩熟於金源典故，宋儒道學源委，尤多究心，史官有露才自是者，每立言未當，起岩據理竄定，深厚醇雅，理致自足。

translations.literal: Qiyan was versed in Jin-source precedents and the origins of Song Ru learning, which he especially studied; when historiographers showed off talent and self-opinion and their wording was improper, Qiyan revised by reason—deep, mellow, and elegant, sufficient in principle.
translations.idiomatic: He knew Jin precedents and Song Neo-Confucian lineage deeply; when compilers vaunted talent and missed the mark, he revised by reason—writing thick, mellow, and self-sufficient.

sentences.zh: 史成，年始六十有五，遂上疏乞骸骨以歸，後四年卒。

translations.literal: When the histories were complete he was just sixty-five; he submitted a memorial begging bones to return, and four years later died.
translations.idiomatic: When the histories were finished he was sixty-five; he asked to retire and died four years later.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文穆。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Wenmu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Wenmu.

sentences.zh: 起岩面如紫瓊，美髯方頤，而眉目清揚可觀，望而知為雅量君子。

translations.literal: Qiyan's face was like purple jade, with a fine beard and square jaw, yet his brows and eyes were clear and spirited to behold; at a glance one knew him for a man of generous measure.
translations.idiomatic: His face was like purple jade, with a fine beard and square jaw, yet bright brows and eyes—at a glance a man of large spirit.

sentences.zh: 及其臨政決議，意所背鄉，屹若泰山，不可回奪。

translations.literal: When he faced government and decided policy, whatever he opposed stood like Mount Tai and could not be turned back.
translations.idiomatic: In council, whatever he opposed stood like Mount Tai and could not be swayed.

sentences.zh: 或時面折人，面頸發赤，不少恕，廟堂憚之。

translations.literal: At times he would rebuke someone to his face until neck and face flushed red, without sparing— the court feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he rebuked men to their faces until he flushed crimson, never sparing; the court stood in awe.

sentences.zh: 識者謂其外和中剛，不受人籠絡，如歐陽修，名聞四裔。

translations.literal: Those who knew him said that outwardly mild and inwardly firm, not subject to others' nets, like Ouyang Xiu—his name was heard in the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Observers said he was mild outside and firm within, not to be coerced—like Ouyang Xiu—and his fame reached the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 安南修貢，其陪臣致其世子之辭，必候起岩起居。

translations.literal: When Annan sent tribute, its attendant envoys presenting the heir's message always waited on Qiyan's health.
translations.idiomatic: When Annam sent tribute, its envoys presenting the crown prince's message always inquired after Qiyan's health first.

sentences.zh: 性孝友，少處窮約，下帷教授，躬致米百里外，以養父母；

translations.literal: By nature filial and friendly, in youth he lived in poverty, drew the curtain to teach, and personally brought rice from a hundred li away to support his parents;
translations.idiomatic: Filial and brotherly by nature, he lived poor in youth, taught behind closed curtains, and walked a hundred li to bring rice for his parents;

sentences.zh: 撫弟如石，教之宦學，無不備至。

translations.literal: he nurtured his younger brother like stone and taught him office and learning, omitting nothing.
translations.idiomatic: he raised his younger brother steadfastly, schooling him for office and learning without stint.

sentences.zh: 舉親族弗克葬者二十餘喪，且買田以給其祭。

translations.literal: He buried more than twenty kin who could not afford funerals and bought fields to supply their sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He buried more than twenty kinsmen who could not afford funerals and bought fields for their sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 凡獲俸賜，必與故人賓客共之。

translations.literal: Whenever he received salary or gifts he always shared them with old friends and guests.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever salary or gifts he received he shared with old friends and guests.

sentences.zh: 卒之日，廩無餘粟，家無餘財。

translations.literal: On the day he died the granary had no surplus grain and the house no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the granary held no surplus grain and the house no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 先是，至元乙酉三月乙亥，太史奏文昌星明，文運將興。

translations.literal: Earlier, on the yihai day of the third month of yiyou in the Zhiyuan era, the Grand Astrologer reported the Wenchang star bright and the literary fortune about to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, on the third month's yihai day of Zhiyuan's yiyou year, the grand astrologer reported Wenchang bright and literary fortune rising.

sentences.zh: 時世祖行幸上京，明日丙子，皇孫降生於儒州。

translations.literal: At that time Shizu was traveling to Shangdu; the next day, bingzi, the imperial grandson was born at Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu was then at Shangdu; next day, bingzi, the imperial grandson was born at Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 是夜，起岩亦生。

translations.literal: That night Qiyan was also born.
translations.idiomatic: That same night Qiyan was born.

sentences.zh: 其後皇孫踐祚，是為仁宗，始詔設科取士，及廷試，起岩遂為第一人，論者以為非偶然也。

translations.literal: Afterward the imperial grandson ascended the throne—this was Renzong—who first ordered the civil service examinations; at the palace examination Qiyan was first place; discussants held it was no accident.
translations.idiomatic: The grandson later reigned as Emperor Renzong, restored examinations, and at the palace test Qiyan ranked first—commentators called it no accident.

sentences.zh: 起岩博學有文，善篆、隸，有《華峰漫稿》、《華峰類稿》、《金陵集》各若干卷，藏於家。

translations.literal: Qiyan was broadly learned and literary, skilled in seal and clerical script, and had several volumes each of Huafeng Miscellany, Huafeng Classified Drafts, and Jinling Collection, kept at home.
translations.idiomatic: He was learned and literary, skilled in seal and clerical script, and left Huafeng Miscellany, Huafeng Classified Drafts, and Jinling Collection in several volumes at home.

sentences.zh: 子二人：琳，琛。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Lin and Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Lin and Chen.

sentences.zh: ○歐陽玄

translations.literal: ○ Ouyang Xuan
translations.idiomatic: ○ Ouyang Xuan

sentences.zh: 歐陽玄，字原功，其先家廬陵，與文忠公修同所自出。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xuan, styled Yuangong; his ancestors' home was Luling, of the same descent as the Duke of Letters Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xuan, styled Yuangong, came from Luling, the same line as Ouyang Xiu the Duke of Letters.

sentences.zh: 至曾大父新，始遷居瀏陽，故玄為瀏陽人。

translations.literal: By his great-great-grandfather Xin the family first moved to Liuyang, so Xuan was a man of Liuyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Xin first moved the family to Liuyang, so Xuan was counted a Liuyang man.

sentences.zh: 幼岐嶷，母李氏，親授《孝經》、《論語》、小學諸書，八歲能成誦，始從鄉先生張貫之學，日記數千言，即知屬文。

translations.literal: In youth he was precocious; his mother Lady Li personally taught the Classic of Filial Piety, Analects, Elementary Learning, and other books; at eight he could recite them complete; he then studied under the village teacher Zhang Guan, recording several thousand words a day, and at once knew how to compose.
translations.idiomatic: Precocious as a boy, his mother Lady Li taught him the Filial Classic, Analects, Elementary Learning, and more; at eight he recited them by heart; under Zhang Guan he wrote thousands of words a day and soon composed essays.

sentences.zh: 十歲，有黃冠師注目視玄，謂貫之曰：「是兒神氣凝遠，目光射人，異日當以文章冠世，廊廟之器也。

translations.literal: At ten a Daoist priest fixed his gaze on Xuan and said to Guan: "This boy's spirit is concentrated and far-reaching, his eyes shoot forth light; another day he will crown the world in letters—material for the hall and temple."
translations.idiomatic: At ten a Daoist priest stared at Xuan and told Guan, "The boy's spirit is far and keen, his gaze piercing; one day his writing will crown the age—he is hall-and-temple timber."

sentences.zh: 」言訖而去，亟追與語，已失所之。

translations.literal: " When he finished speaking he left; they hurried after to speak with him but had already lost track of him.
translations.idiomatic: " He left at once; they ran to speak with him but he was gone.

sentences.zh: 部使者行縣，玄以諸生見，命賦梅花詩，立成十首，晚歸，增至百首，見者駭異之。

translations.literal: When the branch commissioner toured the county, Xuan met him as a student; ordered to compose poems on plum blossom, he finished ten on the spot; returning in the evening he increased them to a hundred—those who saw were startled.
translations.idiomatic: When the branch commissioner visited the county, Xuan as a student was told to write plum-blossom poems and finished ten at once; that evening he raised them to a hundred and astonished onlookers.

sentences.zh: 年十四，益從宋故老習為詞章，下筆輒成章，每試庠序，輒佔高等。

translations.literal: At fourteen he further studied literary composition with old Song scholars; his brush at once formed chapters; whenever he tested at the school, he always took high rank.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he studied composition with Song veterans; his brush flowed into chapters; in every school examination he took top place.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，下帷數年，人莫見其面。

translations.literal: At the weak-crown year he drew the curtain for several years and no one saw his face.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he shut his door for years and scarcely showed his face.

sentences.zh: 經史百家，靡不研究，伊、洛諸儒源委，尤為淹貫。

translations.literal: The hundred schools of classics and history—none he did not investigate; the origins of the Yi and Luo scholars he especially mastered.
translations.idiomatic: Classics and histories of every school he studied; the Yi and Luo masters he knew through and through.

sentences.zh: 召為國子博士，升國子監丞。

translations.literal: He was summoned as National University Erudite and promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as national university erudite and promoted vice director of the directorate of education.

sentences.zh: 致和元年，遷翰林待制，兼國史院編修官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhihe he was transferred to Hanlin Attendant Draftsman and concurrently Compiler at the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhihe 1 he became Hanlin attendant draftsman and historiography compiler.

sentences.zh: 時當兵興，玄領印攝院事，日直內廷，參決機務，凡遠近調發，制詔書檄。

translations.literal: At that time warfare had arisen; Xuan took the seal and acted as head of the institute, daily attending the inner court and participating in deciding urgent affairs—all distant and near dispatch, edicts, and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: War had broken out; Xuan took charge of the historiography institute, attended court daily, and decided urgent business—all dispatches, edicts, and proclamations.

sentences.zh: 既而改元天歷，郊廟、建後、立儲、肆赦之文，皆經撰述。

translations.literal: Then the era name was changed to Tianli; texts for suburban sacrifice, establishing the empress, establishing the heir, and general amnesty were all drafted by him.
translations.idiomatic: When the era became Tianli, he drafted the suburban rites, empress installation, heir establishment, and amnesty.

sentences.zh: 复條時政數十事，實封以聞，多推行之。

translations.literal: He again listed several dozen current-policy items, sealed them, and submitted them; many were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He listed dozens of policy reforms, sealed and submitted them; many were adopted.

sentences.zh: 明年，初置奎章閣學士院，又置藝文監隸焉，皆選清望官居之，文宗親署玄為藝文少監。

translations.literal: The next year the Kui Zhang Hall Academy of Academicians was first established, and the Bureau of Arts was also placed under it, all filled by officials of clear reputation; Wenzong personally signed Xuan as Vice Director of Arts.
translations.idiomatic: Next year the Kui Zhang academy was founded with an arts bureau under it, staffed by men of standing; Wenzong personally appointed Xuan vice director of arts.

sentences.zh: 奉詔纂修《經世大典》，升太監、檢校書籍事。

translations.literal: By imperial order he compiled the Comprehensive Institutions of Government Through the Ages, was promoted to Grand Director and Proofreader of Books.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to compile the Comprehensive Institutions, he rose to grand director and proofreader of books.

sentences.zh: 元統元年，改僉太常禮儀院事，拜翰林直學士，編修四朝實錄，俄兼國子祭酒，召赴中都議事，升侍講學士，复兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong he was changed to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, appointed Hanlin Direct Academician, compiled the Veritable Records of four reigns, soon also Chancellor of the National University, summoned to the Central Capital for deliberation, promoted Academician Expositor, and again concurrently Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuantong 1 he became vice director of imperial sacrifices, Hanlin direct academician, compiler of four reigns' veritable records, then also chancellor of the national university, was summoned to the central capital, made expositor, and again chancellor of the university.

sentences.zh: 重紀至元五年，足患風痺，乞南歸以便醫藥，帝不允。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of the Zhizheng era of the Chongji reign, his feet suffered wind paralysis; he begged to return south for medicine and the emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongji Zhizheng 5 his legs were paralyzed by wind; he asked to go south for treatment and the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 拜翰林學士，未幾，懇辭去位，帝復不允，免其行朝賀禮。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin Academician; before long he earnestly begged to leave office; the emperor again did not grant it and exempted him from court congratulation rites.
translations.idiomatic: Made Hanlin academician, he soon begged to resign; the emperor again refused but excused him from congratulatory audiences.

sentences.zh: 至正改元，更張朝政，事有不便者，集議廷中，玄極言無隱，科目之复，沮者尤眾，玄尤力爭之。

translations.literal: When the Zhengzheng era began and court government was renewed, whenever something was inconvenient they gathered to discuss in court; Xuan spoke without concealment; on restoring the examinations the obstructors were especially many, and Xuan argued all the more forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: At the Zhengzheng renewal, matters disputed in court drew his blunt speech; on restoring civil examinations opposition was fierce and he argued hardest.

sentences.zh: 未幾南歸，復起為翰林學士，以疾未行。

translations.literal: Before long he returned south; he was again raised as Hanlin Academician but did not go because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he went south, was recalled as Hanlin academician, but illness kept him from traveling.

sentences.zh: 詔修遼、金、宋三史，召為總裁官，發凡舉例，俾論撰者有所據依。

translations.literal: An edict ordered compilation of the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song; he was summoned as Chief Compiler, set out principles and examples, and enabled the compilers to have something to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to compile the Liao, Jin, and Song histories, he was chief compiler, laid down principles, and gave the writers a standard.

sentences.zh: 史官中有悻悻露才、論議不公者，玄不以口舌爭，俟其呈稿，援筆竄定之，統係自正。

translations.literal: Among the historiographers were those resentful and showing off talent with unfair discussion; Xuan did not dispute with words but waited for their drafts and revised with the brush—the lineage corrected itself.
translations.idiomatic: Some compilers were resentful and unfair; Xuan did not argue but revised their drafts until the lineage stood straight.

sentences.zh: 至於論、贊、表、奏，皆玄屬筆。

translations.literal: As for discussions, eulogies, tables, and memorials, all were drafted by Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Discussions, eulogies, tables, and memorials were all his pen.

sentences.zh: 五年，帝以玄歷仕累朝，且有修三史功，諭旨丞相，超授爵秩，遂擬拜翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the emperor, because Xuan had served through many reigns and had the merit of compiling the three histories, instructed the chancellor to grant rank beyond the norm, and they proposed appointing him Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 the emperor, noting his service through many reigns and compiling the three histories, told the chancellor to advance him beyond rule and proposed him recipient of edicts.

sentences.zh: 及入奏，上稱快者再三。

translations.literal: When he entered to report, the emperor expressed delight again and again.
translations.idiomatic: When he reported in audience, the emperor expressed delight again and again.

sentences.zh: 已而乞致仕，帝復不允。

translations.literal: Before long he begged to retire and the emperor again did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to retire and the emperor again refused.

sentences.zh: 御史臺奏除福建廉訪使，行次浙西，疾復作，乃上休致之請，作南山隱居，優游山水之間，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: The Censorate memorialized appointing him Surveillance Commissioner of Fujian; traveling through Western Zhe his illness recurred; he then submitted a request to retire, built South Mountain Hermitage, and wandered at ease among mountains and waters with the will to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate proposed him Fujian surveillance commissioner; in Western Zhe his illness returned; he asked to retire, built South Mountain Hermitage, and meant to end his days among hills and streams.

sentences.zh: 復拜翰林學士承旨，玄屢力辭，不獲命。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts; Xuan repeatedly argued forcefully but did not receive the order.
translations.idiomatic: Again made recipient of edicts, Xuan repeatedly declined but could not refuse.

sentences.zh: 奉敕定國律，尋乞致仕，陳情懇切，乃特授湖廣行中書省右丞致仕，賜白玉束帶，給俸賜以終其身。

translations.literal: By imperial order he fixed the national code; soon he begged to retire; his plea was earnest, and he was specially appointed Right Vice Administrator of the Huguang Branch Secretariat in retirement, granted a white jade belt, and given salary and gifts for life.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to fix the national code, he then begged retirement in earnest terms and was specially made right vice administrator of the Huguang branch in retirement, with white jade belt and salary for life.

sentences.zh: 將行，帝复降旨不允，仍前翰林學士承旨，進階光祿大夫。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart the emperor again sent an edict not granting it, keeping him as before as Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts and advancing him to Grand Master for Imperial Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: As he was leaving the emperor again refused, kept him recipient of edicts, and advanced him to grand master for imperial brightness.

sentences.zh: 十四年，汝潁盜起，蔓延南北，州縣幾無完城。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year bandits rose in Ru and Ying and spread north and south; prefectures and counties almost had no intact walls.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 bandits rose in Ru and Ying and spread; few prefectures and counties kept intact walls.

sentences.zh: 玄獻招捕之策千餘言，鑿鑿可行，當時不能用。

translations.literal: Xuan submitted a plan for recruiting and suppressing of more than a thousand words, solid and feasible, but at the time it could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan submitted a thousand-word plan to recruit and suppress rebels, sound and feasible, but it went unused.

sentences.zh: 十七年春，乞致仕，以中原道梗，欲由蜀還鄉，帝復不允。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventeenth year he begged to retire; because the roads of the Central Plain were blocked he wished to return home by Shu; the emperor again did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 17 he asked to retire; central roads were blocked and he wished to go home through Shu; the emperor again refused.

sentences.zh: 時將大赦天下，宣赴內府。

translations.literal: At that time a great amnesty was about to be proclaimed for all under Heaven; he was ordered to announce it at the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: A great amnesty was imminent and he was ordered to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 玄久病，不能步履，丞相傳旨，肩輿至延春閣下，實異數也。

translations.literal: Xuan had long been ill and could not walk; the chancellor transmitted the edict and he was carried in a sedan to below the Yanchun Pavilion—truly an exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: Long ill and unable to walk, he was carried by sedan to the Yanchun Pavilion by the chancellor's order—an exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 是歲十二月戊戌，卒於崇教里之寓舍，年八十五。

translations.literal: On the wuxu day of the twelfth month of that year he died at his lodging in Chongjiao Lane, aged eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth month's wuxu day he died at his Chongjiao Lane lodging, aged eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 中書以聞，帝賜賻甚厚，贈崇仁昭德推忠守正功臣、大司徒、柱國，追封楚國公，諡曰文。

translations.literal: The Central Secretariat reported it; the emperor gave very thick funeral gifts, posthumously enfeoffed him as Grandee of the Court with the title Chongren Zhaode Tuizhong Shouzheng Meritorious Minister, Grand Preceptor, Pillar of the State, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Chu with the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The secretariat reported his death; the emperor gave lavish funeral gifts, enfeoffed him grand preceptor and pillar of the state, duke of Chu with posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 玄性度雍容，含弘縝密，處己儉約，為政廉平。

translations.literal: Xuan's nature was easy and dignified, inclusive and meticulous; in self-conduct he was frugal, in government fair and clean.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was dignified and magnanimous, meticulous in counsel, frugal in private life, and impartial in office.

sentences.zh: 歷官四十餘年，在朝之日，殆四之三。

translations.literal: In office more than forty years, days in court were nearly four-fifths of them.
translations.idiomatic: He served over forty years, spending nearly three-quarters of that time at court.

sentences.zh: 三任成均，而兩為祭酒，六入翰林，而三拜承旨。

translations.literal: Three times he held the Directorate of Education and twice was Chancellor; six times he entered the Hanlin and thrice was appointed Recipient of Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Thrice he led the directorate of education and twice was its chancellor; six times he entered the Hanlin and thrice became recipient of edicts.

sentences.zh: 修實錄、《大典》、三史，皆大製作。

translations.literal: Compiling the Veritable Records, the Comprehensive Institutions, and the three histories were all great undertakings.
translations.idiomatic: Editing veritable records, the Comprehensive Institutions, and the three histories were all major works.

sentences.zh: 屢主文衡，兩知貢舉及讀卷官，凡宗廟朝廷雄文大冊、播告萬方制誥，多出玄手。

translations.literal: He repeatedly presided over literary examinations, twice served as examiner and reader of papers; all grand texts of ancestral temple and court, and edicts proclaimed to the ten thousand directions, mostly came from Xuan's hand.
translations.idiomatic: He often chaired examinations, twice oversaw recruitment and reading papers; state liturgies and edicts to the realm largely came from his pen.

sentences.zh: 金繒上尊之賜，幾無虛歲。

translations.literal: Gold and silk gifts of highest honor—almost no year was empty.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial gifts of gold and silk scarcely missed a year.

sentences.zh: 海內名山大川，釋、老之宮，王公貴人墓隧之碑，得玄文辭以為榮。

translations.literal: Famous mountains and great rivers within the seas, Buddhist and Daoist temples, and tomb steles of kings, dukes, and nobles—all counted it glory to obtain Xuan's literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains, rivers, Buddhist and Daoist shrines, and noble tomb inscriptions prized his writing as an honor.

sentences.zh: 片言隻字，流傳人間，咸知寶重。

translations.literal: A phrase or a single character circulating among the people—all knew to treasure them.
translations.idiomatic: Even a line or a character of his, once abroad, was treasured.

sentences.zh: 文章道德，卓然名世。

translations.literal: In letters and moral conduct he stood eminent in the age.
translations.idiomatic: In literature and conduct he stood eminent in his age.

sentences.zh: 羽儀斯文，贊衛治具，與有功焉。

translations.literal: He adorned civil culture, assisted and guarded the instruments of government, and shared in the achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He adorned letters, upheld governance, and shared in its achievement.

sentences.zh: 玄無子，以從子達老後，复先玄卒。

translations.literal: Xuan had no son; he took his nephew Dala as heir, who again died before Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, he adopted his nephew Dala as heir, who predeceased him.

sentences.zh: 有《圭齋文集》若干卷，傳於世。

translations.literal: He had several volumes of Guizhai Collected Works, transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Guizhai Collected Works in several volumes circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: ○許有壬

translations.literal: ○ Ouyang Xuan
translations.idiomatic: ○ Ouyang Xuan

sentences.zh: 許有壬，字可用，其先世居潁，後徙湯陰。

translations.literal: Xu Youren, styled Keyong; his ancestors first dwelt in Ying and later moved to Tangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Youren, styled Keyong, came from Ying and later Tangyin.

sentences.zh: 有壬幼穎悟，讀書一目五行，嘗閱衡州《淨居院碑》，文近千言，一覽輒背誦無遺。

translations.literal: Youren was clever in youth; in reading he took in five lines at a glance. Once he read the Hengzhou Jingju Monastery Stele of nearly a thousand words and after one reading could recite it without omission.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was brilliant, reading five lines at a glance; he once read the thousand-word Hengzhou Jingju Monastery Stele and recited it entire after a single pass.

sentences.zh: 年二十，暢師文薦入翰林，不報，授開寧路學正，升教授，未上，辟山北廉訪司書吏。

translations.literal: At twenty Chang Shiwen recommended him to the Hanlin but there was no response; he was appointed Instructor of Kaining Circuit, promoted to Professor, but before taking office was recruited as clerk of the Shanbei Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty Chang Shiwen recommended him to the Hanlin without result; he became Kaining circuit instructor, then professor, but before reporting was recruited as Shanbei surveillance clerk.

sentences.zh: 擢延祐二年進士第，授同知遼州事。

translations.literal: He was selected in the jinshi examination of the second year of Yanyou and appointed Associate Administrator of Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Yanyou 2 and became associate administrator of Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 會關中有警，鄰州聽民出避，棄孩嬰滿道上，有壬獨率弓箭手，閉城門以守，卒獲無虞。

translations.literal: When alarm arose in Guanzhong, neighboring prefectures allowed the people to flee; abandoned infants filled the roads. Youren alone led archers, closed the city gates to defend, and in the end suffered no harm.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanzhong alarmed, neighbors let people flee and abandoned infants littered the roads; Youren alone led archers, shut the gates, and kept the city safe.

sentences.zh: 州有追逮，不許胥隸足跡至村疃，唯給信牌，令執裡役者呼之，民安而事集。

translations.literal: When the prefecture had arrests, clerks' footprints were not allowed to reach villages; only tokens were given and village officers were made to summon people—the people were at ease and affairs were settled.
translations.idiomatic: For arrests he barred clerks from villages, issued tokens, and had village officers summon suspects—keeping the people calm and business orderly.

sentences.zh: 右族貪虐者懲之，冤獄雖有成案，皆平翻而釋其罪，州遂大治。

translations.literal: He punished greedy and cruel great clans; even wrongful cases already decided he overturned and released, and the prefecture was greatly governed.
translations.idiomatic: He punished predatory clans, reversed settled wrongful cases, and brought the prefecture to good order.

sentences.zh: 六年己未，除山北​​廉訪司經歷。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, jiwei, he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Shanbei.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6, jiwei, he became Shanbei surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 至治元年，遷吏部主事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizhi 1 he became director of personnel.

sentences.zh: 二年，轉江南行台監察御史，行部廣東，以貪墨劾罷廉訪副使哈只蔡衍。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Investigating Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat, toured Guangdong, and impeached and dismissed Vice Surveillance Commissioner Haizhi Caiyan for bribery.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he became Jiangnan investigating censor, toured Guangdong, and impeached vice surveillance commissioner Haizhi Caiyan for corruption.

sentences.zh: 至江西，會廉訪使苗好謙監焚昏鈔，檢視鈔者日至百餘人，好謙恐其有弊，痛鞭之。

translations.literal: Reaching Jiangxi, he met Surveillance Commissioner Miao Haoqian supervising the burning of worn notes; those inspecting notes came to more than a hundred a day. Haoqian feared fraud and flogged them severely.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangxi he found surveillance commissioner Miao Haoqian burning worn notes; over a hundred inspectors came daily, and fearing fraud Miao flogged them harshly.

sentences.zh: 人畏罪，率剔真為偽，以迎其意。

translations.literal: People feared punishment and generally stripped genuine notes to make false ones to please his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified of punishment, they often stripped genuine notes to forge false ones to please him.

sentences.zh: 筦庫吏而下，榜掠無全膚，迄莫能償。

translations.literal: From treasury clerks downward, beating left no whole skin, and in the end they could not make restitution.
translations.idiomatic: Treasury clerks down were beaten until raw and still could not make restitution.

sentences.zh: 有壬覆視之，率真物也，遂釋之。

translations.literal: Youren re-examined them and found them generally genuine, and then released them.
translations.idiomatic: Youren re-examined the notes, found them genuine, and released the men.

sentences.zh: 凡勢官豪民，人畏之如虎狼者，有壬悉擒治以法，部內肅然。

translations.literal: Whatever powerful officials and great families people feared like tigers and wolves, Youren seized and punished by law, and within the department all was solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful bullies he seized and punished by law until the circuit was quiet.

sentences.zh: 召拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，英宗暴崩於南坡，賊臣鐵失遣使者自上京至，封府庫，收百官印，有壬知事急，即往告御史中丞董守庸，守庸謂宮禁事，非子所當問。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year Emperor Yingzong suddenly died at Nanpo; the traitor minister Teshi sent envoys from Shangdu, sealed the treasuries, and collected the seals of the hundred officials. Youren knew affairs were urgent and at once went to tell Vice Censor-in-Chief Dong Shouyong; Shouyong said palace matters were not what he should ask about.
translations.idiomatic: In month 8 of year 3 Emperor Yingzong died suddenly at Nanpo; traitor Teshi sent envoys from Shangdu, sealed treasuries, and seized official seals. Youren warned vice censor-in-chief Dong Shouyong, who said palace affairs were none of his business.

sentences.zh: 有壬即疏守庸及經歷朵爾只班、監察御史郭也先忽都阿附鐵失之罪以俟。

translations.literal: Youren at once memorialized Shouyong and Commissioner Duoerzhiban and Investigating Censor Guo Yexian Hudou for attaching themselves to Teshi, to await judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Youren memorialized Shouyong, commissioner Duoerzhiban, and censor Guo Yexian Hudou for siding with Teshi, to await judgment.

sentences.zh: 十月，鐵失伏誅。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Teshi was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Teshi was executed.

sentences.zh: 泰定帝發上都，御史大夫紐澤先還京師，有壬即袖疏上之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiding set out from Shangdu; Censor-in-Chief Niuzhe returned first to the capital, and Youren at once presented a memorial from his sleeve.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiding left Shangdu; censor-in-chief Niuzhe returned first to the capital and Youren submitted a memorial from his sleeve.

sentences.zh: 及帝至，复上章言：「帖木迭兒之子瑣南，與聞大逆，乞賜典刑。

translations.literal: When the emperor arrived, he again submitted a memorial saying: "Temuder's son Suonan shared in the great treason—beg that statutory punishment be granted.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor arrived he memorialized again: "Temuder's son Suonan shared the great treason—grant him statutory punishment.

sentences.zh: 其兄弟勿令出入宮禁。

translations.literal: His brothers must not be allowed to enter or leave the palace precincts.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers must not enter or leave the palace precincts.

sentences.zh: 中書平章政事王毅、右丞高昉，橫罹奪爵，而四川行省平章政事趙世延，受禍尤慘，皆請雪冤復職。

translations.literal: Central Secretariat Administrator Wang Yi and Right Administrator Gao Fang were wrongly stripped of rank, while Sichuan Branch Administrator Zhao Shiyan suffered even more cruelly—all begged that wrongs be cleared and offices restored.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator Wang Yi and right administrator Gao Fang were wrongly disgraced, while Sichuan administrator Zhao Shiyan suffered worse—all sought rehabilitation.

sentences.zh: 」繼上正始十事：一曰輔翼太子，宜先訓導；

translations.literal: " He then submitted the Ten Matters of Correct Beginnings: first, in assisting the heir apparent, instruction should come first;
translations.idiomatic: " He then submitted ten reform items: first, instruct the heir apparent before all else;

sentences.zh: 二曰遴選長官，宜先培養；

translations.literal: second, in selecting chief officials, cultivation should come first;
translations.idiomatic: second, cultivate chief officials before appointing them;

sentences.zh: 三曰通籍宮禁，宜別貴賤；

translations.literal: third, in registry at the palace, noble and common should be distinguished;
translations.idiomatic: third, distinguish ranks for palace registry;

sentences.zh: 四曰欲謹兵權，宜削兼領；

translations.literal: fourth, if one wishes to tighten military authority, concurrent commands should be cut;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, to tighten military authority, end concurrent commands;

sentences.zh: 五曰武備廢弛，宜加修飭；

translations.literal: fifth, with military preparations neglected, they should be strengthened;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, restore neglected military preparations;

sentences.zh: 六曰賊臣妻妾，宜禁勢官徵索；

translations.literal: sixth, the wives and concubines of traitor ministers should be forbidden to powerful officials for seizure;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, forbid powerful men from seizing traitors' wives;

sentences.zh: 七曰前赦權以止變，宜再詔以正名；

translations.literal: seventh, the earlier amnesty granted as expedient to stop change should be followed by a new edict to set names right;
translations.idiomatic: seventh, follow the expedient amnesty with a new edict to set names right;

sentences.zh: 八曰帖木迭兒諸子，宜籍沒以懲惡；

translations.literal: eighth, Temuder's sons should have property confiscated to punish wickedness;
translations.idiomatic: eighth, confiscate Temuder's sons' property to punish wickedness;

sentences.zh: 九曰考驗經費，以減民賦；

translations.literal: ninth, examine expenditures to reduce the people's tax burden;
translations.idiomatic: ninth, audit expenditures to lighten taxes;

sentences.zh: 十曰撙節浮蠹，以紓國用。

translations.literal: tenth, restrain floating waste to ease state use.
translations.idiomatic: tenth, cut waste to ease state finances.

sentences.zh: 帝多從之。

translations.literal: The emperor mostly followed them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor largely accepted them.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年，初立詹事院，選為中議，改中書左司員外郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiding the Household of the Heir Apparent was first established; he was selected as Middle Counselor and changed to Left Section Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiding 1, when the heir's household was founded, he became middle counselor, then left-section vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 京畿飢，有壬請賑之。

translations.literal: The capital region suffered famine; Youren requested relief.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital region starved, Youren sought relief.

sentences.zh: 同列讓曰：「子言固善，其如虧國何！

translations.literal: Colleagues reproached him: "Your words are indeed good, but what of harming the state!"
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues objected: "Your plan is good, but what of the state's loss!"

sentences.zh: 」有壬曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Youren said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: " Youren said, "Not so.

sentences.zh: 民，本也，不虧民，顧豈虧國邪！

translations.literal: The people are the root; if the people are not harmed, how could the state be harmed!"
translations.idiomatic: The people are the root; harm not the people and the state cannot be harmed!"

sentences.zh: 」卒白於丞相，發糧四十萬斛濟之，民賴以活者甚眾。

translations.literal: " In the end he reported to the chancellor, grain of four hundred thousand hu was issued to relieve them, and very many people relied on it to live.
translations.idiomatic: " He persuaded the chancellor to issue four hundred thousand hu of grain; multitudes lived by it.

sentences.zh: 國學舊法，每以積分次第貢以出官，執政用監丞張起岩議，欲廢之，而以推擇德行為務。

translations.literal: The old law of the National University advanced men by accumulated points in order for office; the administration, using Supervisor Zhang Qiyan's proposal, wished to abolish it and instead make selection of moral conduct the task.
translations.idiomatic: The university advanced students by accumulated points for office; the administration, following Zhang Qiyan, wished to abolish points and select only by moral conduct.

sentences.zh: 有壬折之曰：「積分雖未盡善，然可得博學能文之士，若曰惟德行之擇，其名固佳，恐皆厚貌深情，專意外飾，或懵不能識丁矣。

translations.literal: Youren refuted it: "Accumulated points, though not wholly good, yet obtain broadly learned and able literary men; if one says only moral conduct is chosen, the name is indeed fine, but I fear all will be thick-faced and deep-hearted, devoted to outward ornament, or stupid and unable to recognize a single character."
translations.idiomatic: Youren objected: "Points are imperfect yet yield learned writers; moral selection sounds fine but may produce hypocrites or men who cannot read."

sentences.zh: 」議久不決。

translations.literal: " Deliberation long went undecided.
translations.idiomatic: " Debate dragged on.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，升右司郎中，其事遂行，已而復寢。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year he was promoted to Right Section Director; the matter then went forward, but soon was again shelved.
translations.idiomatic: In month 6 of year 3 he became right-section director; the reform briefly took effect, then lapsed.

sentences.zh: 獲盜例有賞，論者多疑其偽，有淹四十餘年者，群訴於馬首，有壬曰：「盜賊方熾，求疵太甚，緩急何以使人！

translations.literal: Capturing bandits had rewards by precedent; discussants mostly doubted them as false; some delayed more than forty years, all appealing at his horse's head. Youren said: "Bandits are just now raging; if we seek flaws too finely, how in urgency will we move men!"
translations.idiomatic: Rewards for captured bandits were often doubted as fraud; some cases lingered forty years. Youren said, "Bandits rage now—nitpicking defeats urgency!"

sentences.zh: 但經部使者覆核者，皆予官。

translations.literal: But those rechecked by branch commissioners—all were given office.
translations.idiomatic: Those rechecked by branch commissioners he rewarded with office.

sentences.zh: 」俄移左司郎中，每遇公議，有壬屢爭事得失，汛掃積滯，幾無留牘。

translations.literal: " Soon he was moved to Left Section Director; whenever public discussion arose, Youren repeatedly argued gains and losses, swept accumulated backlog, and almost no documents remained.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon left-section director; in council he argued every point, cleared backlog, and left almost no pending papers.

sentences.zh: 都事宋本退語人曰：「此貞觀、開元間議事也。

translations.literal: Director Song Ben withdrew and told people: "This is deliberation from the Zhenguan and Kaiyuan eras."
translations.idiomatic: Director Song Ben said afterward, "This is council like Zhenguan and Kaiyuan."

sentences.zh: 」明年，丁父憂。

translations.literal: " The next year he mourned his father.
translations.idiomatic: " The next year he mourned his father.

sentences.zh: 天曆三年，擢兩淮都轉運鹽司使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianli he was promoted to Commissioner of the Lianghuai Salt Transport.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianli 3 he became Lianghuai salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 先是，鹽法壞，廷議非有壬不能集事，故有是命。

translations.literal: Earlier the salt law had broken down; court discussion held that without Youren the affair could not be settled, hence this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The salt law had collapsed; court opinion held only Youren could fix it, hence the appointment.

sentences.zh: 有壬詢究弊端，立法而通融之，國課遂登。

translations.literal: Youren investigated abuses, legislated with flexibility, and state revenue then rose.
translations.idiomatic: He investigated abuses, legislated flexibly, and state salt revenue rose.

sentences.zh: 至順二年二月，召參議中書省事，未幾，以丁母憂去。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Zhishun he was summoned as Secretariat Counselor; before long he left for mourning his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhishun 2, month 2, he was summoned as secretariat counselor, then left to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 元統元年，復以參議召。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong he was again summoned as Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuantong 1 he was again summoned as counselor.

sentences.zh: 明年甲戌，拜治書侍御史，轉奎章閣學士院侍書學士，仍治台事。

translations.literal: The next year, jiaxu, he was appointed Investigating Censor-in-Chief, transferred to Academician Expositor of the Kui Zhang Hall Academy, and still managed censorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Next year, jiaxu, he became investigating censor-in-chief, Kui Zhang expositor, and still ran censorate business.

sentences.zh: 會福達魯花赤完卜，藉丞相勢，宿衛東宮，其行頗淫穢，御史劾之，完卜藏御史大夫家，有壬捕而遣之。

translations.literal: The Darughachi Wandu, relying on the chancellor's power, lodged in the Eastern Palace guard; his conduct was quite licentious. Censors impeached him; Wandu hid in the censor-in-chief's house; Youren seized and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Darughachi Wandu, backed by the chancellor, guarded the eastern palace licentiously; censors impeached him; he hid with the censor-in-chief; Youren seized and expelled him.

sentences.zh: 九月，拜中書參知政事、知經筵事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was appointed Secretariat Administrator and Lecturer at the Classics Mat.
translations.idiomatic: In month 9 he became secretariat administrator and classics mat lecturer.

sentences.zh: 帝詔群臣議上皇太后尊號為太皇太后，有壬曰：「皇上於皇太后，母子也，若加太皇太后，則為孫矣，非禮也。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the hundred officials to discuss raising the empress dowager's title to Grand Empress Dowager. Youren said: "The emperor toward the empress dowager is mother and son; if one adds Grand Empress Dowager, he becomes a grandson—this is not ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to raise the empress dowager to grand empress dowager, Youren said, "Mother and son would become grandson and elder—against ritual."

sentences.zh: 」眾弗之從，有壬曰：「今制，封贈祖父母，降於父母一等，蓋推恩之法，近重而遠輕，今尊皇太后為太皇太后，是推而遠之，乃反輕矣，豈所謂尊之者邪！

translations.literal: " The multitude did not follow him. Youren said: "Present regulations enfeoff grandparents one rank below parents—this is the method of extending grace, near heavy and far light. Now honoring the empress dowager as Grand Empress Dowager is pushing away and thus making light—how is this what is called honoring!"
translations.idiomatic: " Overruled, he said, "Enfeoffing grandparents one rank below parents extends grace outward; making her grand empress dowager pushes honor away and lightens it—how is that honoring?"

sentences.zh: 」弗之聽。

translations.literal: " They did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " They would not listen.

sentences.zh: 中書平章政事徹理帖木兒挾私憾，奏罷進士科，有壬廷爭甚苦不能奪，遂稱疾在告，帝強起之，拜侍御史。

translations.literal: Central Secretariat Administrator Cherig Temur bore private resentment and memorialized abolishing the jinshi examinations; Youren argued bitterly in court and could not prevail, then claimed illness and took leave; the emperor forced him up and appointed Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator Cherig Temur abolished the jinshi; Youren argued bitterly in vain, feigned illness, and was forced up as attending censor.

sentences.zh: 會汝寧棒胡反，大臣有忌漢官者，取賊所造旗幟及偽宣敕，班地上，問曰：「此欲何為耶？

translations.literal: When the Bang Hu of Runing rebelled, ministers who resented Han officials took the rebels' banners and forged edicts, spread them on the ground, and asked: "What is this meant to do?"
translations.idiomatic: When Runing's Bang Hu rebelled, ministers hostile to Han officials spread rebel banners and forged edicts on the floor and asked, "What do you make of this?"

sentences.zh: 」意漢官諱言反，將以罪中之。

translations.literal: " Their intent was that Han officials would shrink from speaking of rebellion and they would convict them thereby.
translations.idiomatic: " They meant to trap Han officials who shrank from saying "rebellion."

sentences.zh: 有壬曰：「此曹建年號，稱李老君太子，部署士卒，以敵官軍，其反狀甚明，尚何言！

translations.literal: Youren said: "These fellows established a reign title, called themselves crown prince of Lord Lao, deployed troops to fight the government army—the signs of rebellion are very clear; what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: Youren said, "They proclaimed a reign title, called themselves Lao's crown prince, and fought the army—the rebellion is obvious!"

sentences.zh: 」其語遂塞。

translations.literal: " Their words were then blocked.
translations.idiomatic: " Their trap failed.

sentences.zh: 廷議欲行古劓法，立行樞密院，禁漢人、南人勿學蒙古、畏吾兒字書，有壬皆爭止之。

translations.literal: Court discussion wished to apply the ancient nose-cutting law, establish a mobile Privy Council, and forbid Han and southern people from learning Mongol and Uighur script; Youren argued and stopped them all.
translations.idiomatic: Council proposed nose-cutting, a mobile privy council, and barring Han and southerners from Mongol and Uighur script; Youren stopped all.

sentences.zh: 重紀至元初，長蘆韓公溥因家藏兵器，遂起大獄，株連台若省，多以贓敗，獨無有壬名，由是忌者益甚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongji Zhizheng, Han Gongpu of Changlu raised a great case because of weapons stored at home, implicating the censorate and secretariat; many fell to corruption, but Youren's name alone was not among them, and from this those who resented him grew more.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongji Zhizheng, Han Gongpu of Changlu raised a weapons case implicating censorate and secretariat; many fell for graft, but not Youren—resentment deepened.

sentences.zh: 有壬度不可留，遂歸彰德，已而南游湘、漢間。

translations.literal: Youren judged he could not remain and returned to Zhangde; afterward he traveled south through Xiang and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he could not stay, he returned to Zhangde, then traveled through Xiang and Han.

sentences.zh: 至元六年，召入中書，仍為參知政事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan he was summoned into the Central Secretariat and again made Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 6 he was summoned to the secretariat again as administrator.

sentences.zh: 明年，改元至正，有壬極論帝當親祠太廟，母后虛位，徽政院當罷，改元命相當合為上詔，冗職當沙汰，錢糧當裁節，如此之類，不一而足。

translations.literal: The next year the era was changed to Zhengzheng; Youren argued forcefully that the emperor should personally sacrifice at the Grand Temple, that the empress's seat was empty, that the Huizheng Court should be abolished, that edicts for the change of era and appointment of chancellor should be combined into a supreme edict, that redundant offices should be purged, that money and grain should be cut—matters of this kind, more than could be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Next year, at the Zhengzheng change, he urged personal temple sacrifice, filling the empress's seat, abolishing the Huizheng Court, merging edicts, purging offices, and cutting revenue—among many reforms.

sentences.zh: 人皆韙之。

translations.literal: People all approved.
translations.idiomatic: All approved.

sentences.zh: 轉中書左丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Administrator of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He became left secretariat administrator.

sentences.zh: 二年，囊加慶善八及孛羅帖木兒獻議，開西山金口導渾河，逾京城，達通州，以通漕運。

translations.literal: In the second year Nanggasanba and Bolu Temur offered a plan to open the Jinkou of West Mountain to channel the Hun River past the capital to Tongzhou for grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 Nanggasanba and Bolu Temur proposed opening West Mountain's Jinkou to divert the Hun River through the capital to Tongzhou for grain transport.

sentences.zh: 丞相脫脫主之甚力，有壬曰：「渾河之水，湍悍易決，而足以為害，淤淺易塞，而不可行舟；

translations.literal: Chancellor Toqtoq supported it with great force. Youren said: "The waters of the Hun River are violent and easy to burst, sufficient to do harm; silted and shallow, easy to block, and unsuitable for boats;
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Toqtoq backed it fiercely. Youren said, "The Hun is violent and prone to burst, shallow and prone to silt, unfit for shipping;

sentences.zh: 況地勢高下，甚有不同，徒勞民費財耳。

translations.literal: moreover the terrain high and low differs greatly—only laboring the people and wasting wealth."
translations.idiomatic: and the terrain varies—this only wastes labor and treasure."

sentences.zh: 」不聽，後卒如有壬言。

translations.literal: " They did not listen; afterward it ended as Youren had said.
translations.idiomatic: " They refused; events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 先是，有壬之父熙載仕長沙日，設義學，訓諸生。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Youren's father Xizai served at Changsha he established a charity school to instruct students.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, his father Xizai at Changsha founded a charity school.

sentences.zh: 既歿，而諸生思之，為立東岡書院，朝廷賜額設官，以為育才之地。

translations.literal: After he died the students missed him and built Donggang Academy; the court granted a plaque and established officials as a place to nurture talent.
translations.idiomatic: After his death students built Donggang Academy; the court granted a plaque and officials to nurture talent.

sentences.zh: 南台監察御史木八剌沙，緣睚眥怨，言書院不當立，並構浮辭，誣衊有壬，併其二弟有儀、有孚，有壬遂稱病歸。

translations.literal: Southern Branch Investigating Censor Mubalasha, from a grudge, said the academy should not stand and also fabricated slander against Youren, together with his two younger brothers Youyi and Youfu; Youren then claimed illness and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Southern censor Mubalasha, grudging him, attacked the academy and slandered Youren and brothers Youyi and Youfu; Youren retired ill.

sentences.zh: 四年，改江浙行省左丞，辭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made Left Administrator of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat and declined.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was offered Jiangzhe left administrator and declined.

sentences.zh: 六年，召為翰林學士，既上，又辭。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned as Hanlin Academician; having reported in, he again declined.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was summoned Hanlin academician, reported, and declined again.

sentences.zh: 監察御史累章辨其誣。

translations.literal: Investigating censors repeatedly memorialized to clear the slander.
translations.idiomatic: Censors repeatedly cleared the slander.

sentences.zh: 俄拜浙西廉訪使，未上，復以翰林學士承旨召，仍知經筵事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Western Zhe; before taking office he was again summoned as Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts, still Lecturer at the Classics Mat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon made Western Zhe surveillance commissioner, but before reporting was recalled as Hanlin recipient of edicts and classics mat lecturer.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，授御史中丞，賜白玉束帶及御衣一襲，未幾，復以病歸。

translations.literal: The next summer he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief, granted a white jade belt and one suit of imperial robes; before long he again returned for illness.
translations.idiomatic: Next summer he became vice censor-in-chief with white jade belt and imperial robes, then soon retired ill again.

sentences.zh: 監察御史答蘭不花銜有壬，時短長之，奏劾甚力，事尋白。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Dalan Buhua bore resentment toward Youren and at times spoke ill of him, memorializing impeachment with great force; the affair was soon cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Dalan Buhua impeached him fiercely from resentment; the charge soon failed.

sentences.zh: 十二年，盜起河南，聲撼河朔間，有壬畫備御之策十五條，以授郡將，民藉以安。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year bandits rose in Henan and their sound shook the Hebei region; Youren drew fifteen items of defense policy and gave them to the prefectural commanders, and the people relied on them to be secure.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 Henan rebels shook Hebei; Youren drafted fifteen defense measures for commanders, and the people were secured.

sentences.zh: 十三年，起拜河南行省左丞。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was raised and appointed Left Administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he was raised left administrator of the Henan branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣將出征，環河南境，連營以百數，一切芻餉，皆仰給之，有壬從容集事，若平時然。

translations.literal: The court sent generals on campaign; encircling the Henan border, linked camps numbered in the hundreds—all fodder and supplies depended on him; Youren calmly gathered affairs as in normal times.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent armies around Henan in hundreds of camps; all fodder depended on him, yet he managed affairs as calmly as in peacetime.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遷集賢大學士，尋改樞密副使，復拜中書左丞。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents, soon changed to Vice Minister of the Privy Council, and again appointed Left Administrator of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he became grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents, then vice privy council minister, then again left secretariat administrator.

sentences.zh: 時以言為諱，有壬力言朝廷務行姑息之政，賞重罰輕，故將士貪掠子女玉帛而無鬥志，遂倡招降之策，言多不載。

translations.literal: At that time speech was taboo; Youren forcefully said the court pursued indulgent policy, rewards heavy and punishments light, so officers and soldiers plundered women and jade silks without fighting spirit—he then advocated surrender policy, but much was not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Speech was dangerous; he argued the court's indulgence—heavy rewards, light punishments—left troops plundering without fight, and urged surrender policies, much unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 有僧名開，自高郵來，言張士誠乞降，眾幸事且成，皆大喜，有壬獨疑其妄，呼僧詰之，果語塞不能對。

translations.literal: A monk named Kai came from Gaoyou saying Zhang Shicheng begged to surrender; the multitude hoped the affair would succeed and all rejoiced; Youren alone doubted it false, called the monk to question him, and indeed he was speechless and could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: A monk named Kai from Gaoyou claimed Zhang Shicheng would surrender; all rejoiced, but Youren doubted him, questioned him, and the monk could not answer.

sentences.zh: 轉集賢大學士，兼太子左諭德，階至光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents, concurrently Left Tutor of the Heir Apparent, rank reaching Grand Master for Imperial Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: He became grand academician, left tutor to the heir apparent, and grand master for imperial brightness.

sentences.zh: 有壬前朝舊德，太子頗敬禮之。

translations.literal: Youren was an old worthy of the previous reign; the heir apparent greatly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: An elder of the prior reign, he was greatly respected by the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 一日入見，方臂鷙禽以為樂，遽呼左右屏去。

translations.literal: One day entering audience, the heir was just sporting a fierce bird on his arm for pleasure and at once called attendants to remove it.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he came to audience, the heir was sporting a hawk on his arm and hastily had it taken away.

sentences.zh: 十七年，以老病，力乞致其事，久之始得請，給俸賜以終其身。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, old and ill, he forcefully begged to retire from affairs; only after long delay was it granted, salary and gifts given for life.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17, aged and ill, he begged hard to retire; after long delay he was granted salary for life.

sentences.zh: 二十四年九月二十一日卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day of the ninth month of the twenty-fourth year he died, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-first day of the ninth month of year 24 he died, aged seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 有壬歷事七朝，垂五十年，遇國家大事，無不盡言，皆一根至理，而曲盡人情。

translations.literal: Youren served through seven reigns for nearly fifty years; encountering great affairs of state he never failed to speak fully—all rooted in ultimate principle yet bending to human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Serving seven reigns for nearly fifty years, on every great state matter he spoke fully—grounded in principle yet mindful of human feeling.

sentences.zh: 當權臣恣睢之時，稍忤意，輒誅竄隨之，有壬絕不為巧避計，事有不便，明辨力諍，不知有死生利害，君子多之。

translations.literal: When powerful ministers were overbearing, slight offense brought execution and exile; Youren absolutely would not use crafty evasion; when something was inconvenient he argued clearly and forcefully, heedless of life, gain, or harm—gentlemen mostly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers were overbearing, slight offense meant death or exile; he never dodged craftily, argued bluntly heedless of life or profit, and gentlemen praised him.

sentences.zh: 有壬善筆札，工辭章，歐陽玄序其文，謂其雄渾閎雋，湧如層瀾，迫而求之，則淵靚深實，蓋深許之也。

translations.literal: Youren was skilled at letters and accomplished in literary composition; Ouyang Xuan prefaced his writings, saying they were grand, vast, and powerful, surging like layered billows; pressed to seek them, they were deep, quiet, and solid—he deeply commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in letters and composition, Ouyang Xuan praised his writing as vast and surging yet deep and solid when examined closely.

sentences.zh: 所著有《至正集》若干卷。

translations.literal: His writings include several volumes of the "Zhengzheng Collection".
translations.idiomatic: He left the "Zhengzheng Collection" in several volumes.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文忠。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 子一人，曰禎。

translations.literal: He had one son, named Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He had one son, Zhen.

sentences.zh: ○宋本

translations.literal: ○ Song Ben
translations.idiomatic: ○ Song Ben

sentences.zh: 宋本，字誠夫，大都人。

translations.literal: Song Ben, styled Chengfu, was a man of Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: Song Ben, styled Chengfu, was from Dadu.

sentences.zh: 自幼穎拔異群兒，既成童，聚經史窮日夜讀之，句探字索，必通貫乃已。

translations.literal: From youth he was sharp and stood apart from other children; once grown, he gathered classics and histories and read them day and night, probing sentences and seeking characters, not stopping until he had mastered them through.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he outshone other children; as a youth he read classics and histories day and night until he mastered every line.

sentences.zh: 嘗從父禎官江陵，​​江陵王奎文，明性命義理之學，本往質所得，造詣日深。

translations.literal: Once he followed his father Zhen in office at Jiangling; Wang Kuiwen of Jiangling understood the learning of nature, fate, and moral principle; Ben went to question him and daily deepened his attainment.
translations.idiomatic: Following his father Zhen to Jiangling, he studied nature and moral principle under Wang Kuiwen and deepened daily.

sentences.zh: 善為古文，辭必己出，峻潔刻厲，多微辭。

translations.literal: He was good at ancient-style prose; his wording was always his own, stern, clean, and incisive, often with subtle phrasing.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote ancient-style prose in his own voice—severe, clean, incisive, often subtly allusive.

sentences.zh: 年四十，始還燕。

translations.literal: At forty he first returned to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: At forty he first returned to Yan.

sentences.zh: 至治元年，策天下士於廷，本為第一人，賜進士及第，授翰林修撰。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi the court examined scholars of the realm; Ben was first and was granted jinshi with honors, appointed Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizhi 1 he ranked first in the palace examination, received jinshi with honors, and became Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年春，除監察御史，首言：「逆賊鐵失等雖伏誅，其黨樞密副使阿散，身親弒逆，以告變得不死，竄嶺南，乞早正天討。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Taiding he was appointed Investigating Censor and first said: "Though the traitors Teshi and others were executed, their partisan Vice Minister of the Privy Council Asan personally joined the regicide; by reporting the plot he escaped death and was banished to Lingnan—beg early heavenly punishment."
translations.idiomatic: In Taiding 1 spring he became investigating censor and first urged: "Though Teshi was executed, his partisan Asan joined the regicide yet escaped death by informing—punish him at once."

sentences.zh: 」國製，範黃金為太廟神主，仁宗室盜竟竊去，本言：「在法，民間失盜，捕之違期不獲猶治罪，太常失典守，及在京應捕官，皆當罷去。

translations.literal: " By national regulation, spirit tablets of the Grand Temple were cast in yellow gold; the tablet of Renzong's shrine was actually stolen. Ben said: "By law, when common people lose goods to theft, if capture is overdue and fails they are still punished; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices lost custody, and all arresting officers in the capital should be dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: " National law cast golden spirit tablets for the Grand Temple; Renzong's tablet was stolen. Ben said arrest officers and Court of Imperial Sacrifices custodians must be dismissed, as with overdue theft cases."

sentences.zh: 」又言：「中書宰執，日趨禁中，固寵苟安，兼旬不至中堂，壅滯機務，乞戒飭臣僚，自非入宿衛日，必詣所署治事。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Central Secretariat administrators daily hurry into the forbidden precinct to secure favor and ease; for half a month they do not reach the central hall, blocking urgent business—beg to admonish the hundred officials that except on days of palace guard duty they must go to their offices to conduct affairs."
translations.idiomatic: " He also said secretariat chiefs lingered in the palace half a month without reaching the central hall, blocking business—officials except on guard duty must attend their offices."

sentences.zh: 」皆不報。

translations.literal: " All went unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: " All went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 踰月，調國子監丞。

translations.literal: After a month he was transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he became vice director of the directorate of education.

sentences.zh: 夏，風烈地震，有旨集百官雜議弭災之道。

translations.literal: In summer fierce wind and earthquake struck; an order gathered the hundred officials to discuss mixed ways to quell disaster.
translations.idiomatic: That summer fierce wind and earthquake struck; the court gathered officials to discuss quelling disaster.

sentences.zh: 時宿衛士自北方來者，復遣歸，乃百十為群，剽劫殺人桓州道中。

translations.literal: At that time palace guards returning from the north were sent back again; they banded in groups of tens and hundreds, plundering and killing on the Huanzhou road.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guards returning from the north were sent back and banded in hundreds, plundering and killing on the Huanzhou road.

sentences.zh: 既逮捕，旭滅傑奏釋之。

translations.literal: After arrest, Xumiejie memorialized to release them.
translations.idiomatic: After arrest, Xumiejie memorialized to release them.

sentences.zh: 蒙古千戶使京師​​，宿邸中，適民間硃甲妻女車過邸門，千戶悅之，並從者奪以入，硃泣訴於中書，旭滅傑庇不問。

translations.literal: A Mongol chiliarch came to the capital and lodged at an inn; as commoner Zhu Jia's wife and daughter passed the inn gate in a cart, the chiliarch was pleased and with followers seized them and took them in; Zhu wept and appealed to the Central Secretariat; Xumiejie shielded him and did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: A Mongol chiliarch at an inn seized commoner Zhu Jia's wife and daughter from a passing cart; Zhu appealed to the secretariat but Xumiejie shielded him.

sentences.zh: 本適與議，本復抗言：「鐵失餘黨未誅，仁廟神主盜未得，桓州盜未治，硃甲冤未伸，刑政失度，民憤天怨，災異之見，職此之由。

translations.literal: Ben happened to join the discussion and again spoke forcefully: "Teshi's remnant partisans are not yet executed, Renzong's spirit tablet thief is not yet caught, Huanzhou bandits are not yet punished, Zhu Jia's wrong is not yet redressed—criminal government loses measure, the people resent and Heaven is angry; the appearance of prodigies is due to this."
