translations.idiomatic: Ben argued: "Teshi's partisans remain, the tablet thief is uncaught, Huanzhou bandits unpunished, Zhu's wrong unredressed—hence prodigies and popular wrath."

sentences.zh: 」辭氣激奮，眾皆聳聽。

translations.literal: " His words were excited and forceful; all listened in awe.
translations.idiomatic: " All listened in awe.

sentences.zh: 冬，移兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: In winter he was moved to Vice Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In winter he became vice director of war.

sentences.zh: 二年，轉中書左司都事。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Director of the Left Section of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he became left-section director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會議招撫溪洞民，故將李牢山之子嘗假兵部尚書，從諸王帥兵徵鬱林州徭民，李在道納妾，留不進，兵敗歸，樞密副使王卜鄰吉台言：「李平徭有功，當遷官。

translations.literal: When they met to discuss pacifying the stream-cave people, the son of the former general Li Laoshan had once borrowed the title Minister of War and followed princes leading troops to campaign against the Yao people of Yulin Prefecture; Li on the road took a concubine and lingered without advancing; the army was defeated and he returned; Vice Minister of the Privy Council Wang Bulingjitai said: "Li pacified the Yao with merit and should be promoted."
translations.idiomatic: Discussing pacifying stream-cave peoples, Li Laoshan's son had borrowed the war minister title, dallied with a concubine, lost the Yao campaign, yet Wang Bulingjitai urged promoting him for pacifying the Yao.

sentences.zh: 」本言；

translations.literal: " Ben said:
translations.idiomatic: " Ben said:

sentences.zh: 「李棄軍娶妾，逗撓軍期，宜亟置諸法，況可官邪！

translations.literal: "Li abandoned the army to take a concubine and delayed the campaign schedule—he should quickly be punished by law; how could he be given office!"
translations.idiomatic: "Li abandoned the army for a concubine and delayed the schedule—execute him by law, not promote him!"

sentences.zh: 」王色沮，乃不敢言。

translations.literal: " Wang's color fell and he dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang fell silent.

sentences.zh: 旭滅傑死，左丞相倒剌沙當國得君，與平章政事烏伯都剌，皆西域人，西域富賈以其國異石名曰瓓者來獻，其估巨萬，或未酬其直；

translations.literal: When Xumiejie died, Left Chancellor Toghto held the state and won the ruler's favor, with Administrator Ubaidula—both men of the Western Regions; a rich merchant of the Western Regions brought as tribute a strange stone of their country called lan, valued at tens of thousands, and some had not yet paid its price;
translations.idiomatic: After Xumiejie's death, Toghto and Ubaidula, both Western Region men, ruled; a Western merchant offered a stone called lan worth tens of thousands, often unpaid;

sentences.zh: 諸嘗有過，為司憲褫官，或有出其門下者。

translations.literal: those who had once offended and been stripped of office by the surveillance commission—some came from their faction.
translations.idiomatic: some stripped by the surveillance commission were their clients.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，烏伯都剌自禁中出，至政事堂，集宰執僚佐，命左司員外郎胡彝以詔稿示本，乃以星孛地震赦天下，仍命中書酬累朝所獻諸物之直，擢用自英廟至今為憲台奪官者。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year Ubaidula came from the forbidden precinct to the Hall of Government, gathered administrators and aides, and ordered Left Section Vice Director Hu Yi to show Ben the draft edict—it was to amnesty all under Heaven for the comet and earthquake, still ordering the Central Secretariat to pay the prices of objects presented through successive reigns and promote those stripped by the censorate since Emperor Ying's reign.
translations.idiomatic: Winter of year 3 Ubaidula showed Ben a draft amnesty for comet and earthquake, paying tribute debts and promoting men the censorate had stripped since Yingzong.

sentences.zh: 本讀竟，白曰：「今警災異，而畏獻物未酬直者憤怨，此有司細故，形諸王言，必貽笑天下。

translations.literal: When Ben finished reading he reported: "Now alarmed by prodigies, yet fearing those who presented goods and were not paid their price resent—this is a petty matter of clerks; to put it in a royal pronouncement will surely make the realm laugh."
translations.idiomatic: Ben said fearing unpaid tribute donors in a royal amnesty would make the realm laugh.

sentences.zh: 司憲褫有罪者官，世祖成憲也，今上即位，累詔法世祖，今擢用之，是廢成憲而反汗前詔也，後復有邪佞贓穢者，將治之邪？

translations.literal: Stripping office from the guilty is Shizu's established regulation; the present emperor on accession repeatedly edicted to follow Shizu—now promoting them is abolishing the established regulation and contradicting earlier edicts; afterward if there are again wicked and corrupt men, will you punish them?
translations.idiomatic: Stripping corrupt officers was Kublai's law; promoting them now voided that law—would future villains be punished?

sentences.zh: 置不問邪？

translations.literal: Or set them aside and not inquire?
translations.idiomatic: Or ignored?

sentences.zh: 」宰執聞本言，相視嘆息罷去。

translations.literal: " The administrators hearing Ben's words looked at each other, sighed, and left.
translations.idiomatic: " The administrators sighed and left.

sentences.zh: 明日，宣詔竟，本遂稱疾不出。

translations.literal: The next day the edict was proclaimed; Ben then claimed illness and did not appear.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the edict was proclaimed; Ben feigned illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 四年春，遷禮部郎中。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 4 he became director of rites.

sentences.zh: 天曆元年冬，升吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Tianli he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianli 1 winter he became vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 二年，改禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year he was changed to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he became vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 是年，文宗開奎章閣，置藝文監，檢校書籍，超大監。

translations.literal: That year Wenzong opened the Kui Zhang Hall, established the Bureau of Arts, and made him Proofreader of Books, surpassing the Grand Director.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wenzong opened the Kui Zhang Hall and arts bureau and made him proofreader of books above grand director.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，進奎章閣學士院供奉學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun he was advanced to Academician Attendant of the Kui Zhang Hall Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhishun 1 he became Kui Zhang attendant academician.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，出為河東廉訪副使，將行，擢禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year he was sent out as Vice Surveillance Commissioner of Hedong; as he was about to depart he was promoted to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhishun 2 winter he was sent as Hedong vice surveillance commissioner but before leaving was made minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，寧宗崩，順帝未至，皇太后在興聖宮，正旦，議循故事，行朝賀禮，本言：「宜上表興聖宮，廢大明殿朝賀。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year Emperor Ningzong died and Emperor Shundi had not yet arrived; the empress dowager was at Xingsheng Palace; on New Year's Day they discussed following precedent and performing court congratulation rites. Ben said: "One should submit a memorial at Xingsheng Palace and abolish congratulation at the Daming Hall."
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 winter Ningzong died before Shundi arrived; on New Year's Day Ben urged memorializing Xingsheng Palace and abolishing Daming Hall congratulations.

sentences.zh: 」眾是而從之。

translations.literal: " The multitude approved and followed.
translations.idiomatic: " All agreed.

sentences.zh: 元統元年，兼經筵官，冬，拜陝西行台治書侍御史，不拜，复留為奎章閣學士院承製學士，仍兼經筵官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong he was concurrently Lecturer at the Classics Mat; in winter he was appointed Investigating Censor-in-Chief of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat but did not accept, again retained as Drafting Academician of the Kui Zhang Hall Academy, still concurrently Lecturer at the Classics Mat.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuantong 1 he was classics mat lecturer, offered Shaanxi investigating censor-in-chief but declined, and stayed Kui Zhang drafting academician.

sentences.zh: 二年夏，轉集賢直學士，兼國子祭酒，兼經筵如故。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year he was transferred to Direct Academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents, concurrently Chancellor of the National University, classics mat unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuantong 2 summer he became direct academician, national university chancellor, and kept the classics mat.

sentences.zh: 是年冬十一月二十五日卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: That year on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month he died, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, on the eleventh month's twenty-fifth day, he died at fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 階官自承務郎十轉至太中大夫。

translations.literal: His rank advanced from Junior Service Gentleman through ten steps to Grand Master for Court Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: His rank rose from junior service gentleman through ten steps to grand master for court discussion.

sentences.zh: 本性高抗不屈，持論堅正，制行純白，不可干以私，而篤朋友之義，堅若金鐵，人有片善，稱道不少置，尤以植立斯文自任。

translations.literal: By nature lofty and unyielding, his arguments firm and correct, his conduct pure white, not to be moved by private interest, yet he was devoted to friendship firm as metal and iron; if a man had the slightest good he praised it without stint, especially taking it as his charge to establish civil culture.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty and unyielding, upright and pure, unmoved by private interest, yet devoted in friendship; he praised every slight merit and took establishing letters as his charge.

sentences.zh: 知貢舉，取進士滿百人額；

translations.literal: Presiding over examinations, he took jinshi to the full quota of a hundred;
translations.idiomatic: As examiner he filled the hundred jinshi quota;

sentences.zh: 為讀卷官，增第一甲為三人。

translations.literal: as reader of papers he increased the first class to three men.
translations.idiomatic: as reader he increased first class to three.

sentences.zh: 父官南中，貧，賣宅以去。

translations.literal: When his father served in the south he was poor and sold the house to leave.
translations.idiomatic: When his father served in the south they were poor and sold their house to depart.

sentences.zh: ，居官清慎自持，饘粥至不給。

translations.literal: , in office he maintained himself with pure caution, thin gruel scarcely sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: , in office he lived with pure caution until thin gruel scarcely sufficed.

sentences.zh: 本未弱冠，聚徒以養親，殆二十年，歷仕通顯，猶僦屋以居。

translations.literal: Before the weak-crown year Ben gathered disciples to support his parents for nearly twenty years; through office to high prominence he still rented a house to dwell.
translations.idiomatic: Before twenty he taught to support his parents nearly twenty years; though eminent he still rented his home.

sentences.zh: 及卒，非賻贈幾不能給棺斂，執紼者近二千人，皆縉紳大夫、門生故吏及國子諸生，未嘗有一雜賓，時人榮之。

translations.literal: When he died, without funeral gifts he could scarcely afford the coffin and burial; those holding the mourning cord were nearly two thousand—all gentry grandees, students, old subordinates, and National University students, never a single miscellaneous guest; people of the time honored it.
translations.idiomatic: At death he scarcely afforded burial without gifts; nearly two thousand gentry, students, and officials bore the bier—no stray guests—and the age honored it.

sentences.zh: 本所著有《至治集》四十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: Ben's writings include forty volumes of the "Zhizhi Collection", circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His forty-volume "Zhizhi Collection" circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 諡正獻。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Zhengxian.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title Zhengxian.

sentences.zh: ○謝端

translations.literal: ○ Xie Duan
translations.idiomatic: ○ Xie Duan

sentences.zh: 謝端，字敬德，蜀之遂寧人。

translations.literal: Xie Duan, styled Jingde, was a man of Suining in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Duan, styled Jingde, was from Suining in Shu.

sentences.zh: 宋末，蜀士多避兵江陵，因家焉。

translations.literal: At the end of the Song many Shu scholars fled warfare to Jiangling and thus made their home there.
translations.idiomatic: Late Song Shu scholars fled war to Jiangling and settled there.

sentences.zh: 端幼穎異，五六歲能吟詩，十歲能作賦。

translations.literal: Duan was clever and unusual in youth; at five or six he could recite poetry, at ten compose fu.
translations.idiomatic: Precocious, he recited poetry at five or six and wrote fu at ten.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，與尚書宋本同師，明性理，為古文，又同教授江陵城中，以文學齊名，時號「謝宋」。

translations.literal: At the weak-crown year he studied with the Minister Song Ben under the same teacher, understood nature and principle, wrote ancient prose, and together taught in Jiangling city—equal in literary fame, at the time called "Xie and Song."
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he studied with Song Ben, mastered Neo-Confucian learning and prose, taught with him in Jiangling, and was famed as "Xie and Song."

sentences.zh: 史槓宣慰荊南，數加延禮，薦之姚燧，燧方以文章大名自負，少所許可，以所為文眎端，端一讀，即能指擿其用意所在，燧嘆獎不已，語人：「後二十年，若謝端者，豈易得哉！

translations.literal: Shi Geng pacified Jingnan and repeatedly honored him, recommending him to Yao Sui; Sui then prided himself on literary great fame and rarely approved anyone—he showed Duan his writing; Duan with one reading could point out where his intent lay; Sui sighed in praise without end and told people: "Twenty years hence, how could one easily obtain another like Xie Duan!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Geng of Jingnan honored him and recommended him to Yao Sui, who rarely praised anyone; Duan read Sui's essay once and pinpointed its intent; Sui marveled and said another like Duan would be rare in twenty years.

sentences.zh: 」用薦者署校官，不報。

translations.literal: " By recommendation he was appointed school official; no response.
translations.idiomatic: " Recommended as school official, he received no appointment.

sentences.zh: 科舉法行，就試河南行省，中其舉，以內艱不會試。

translations.literal: When the examination law was implemented he tested at the Henan Branch Secretariat and passed its nomination but because of mourning his mother did not attend the examination.
translations.idiomatic: When examinations began he passed the Henan nomination but missed the exam mourning his mother.

sentences.zh: 延祐五年，乃擢進士乙科。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yanyou he was finally selected in the second class of jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 5 he finally took jinshi second class.

sentences.zh: 授承事郎、潭州路同知湘陰州事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Junior Service Gentleman and Associate Administrator of Xiangyin Prefecture on Tanzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He became junior service gentleman and associate administrator of Xiangyin on Tanzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 歲滿，入為國子博士，遷太常博士。

translations.literal: When his term ended he entered as National University Erudite and was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After his term he became national university erudite, then court of imperial sacrifices erudite.

sentences.zh: 盜入太廟，失第八室黃金主，坐罷去。

translations.literal: Bandits entered the Grand Temple and the golden spirit tablet of the eighth shrine was lost; he sat in dismissal and left.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits stole the eighth shrine's golden tablet from the Grand Temple; he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 端禮官，非典守，不當坐，亦不辨。

translations.literal: Duan was a ritual officer, not a classic custodian, and should not have been punished—yet he also did not argue.
translations.idiomatic: A ritual officer, not a custodian, he should not have been punished, yet he did not argue.

sentences.zh: 尋除翰林修撰，升待制，以選為國子司業，遂為翰林直學士，階太中大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Hanlin Compiler, promoted to Attendant Draftsman, selected as Vice Chancellor of the National University, then made Hanlin Direct Academician, rank Grand Master for Court Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Hanlin compiler, attendant draftsman, national university vice chancellor, then direct academician at grand master for court discussion.

sentences.zh: 端善為政，筮仕湘陰，猾吏束手，不敢舞文法，豪民無賴者遠避去。

translations.literal: Duan was good at government; on first taking office at Xiangyin, crafty clerks were helpless and dared not twist the law; powerful ruffians fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: In office at Xiangyin crafty clerks dared not twist law and ruffians fled.

sentences.zh: 部使者行部，旁郡滯訟，皆諉端讞，端剖決如流，績譽籍然。

translations.literal: When the branch commissioner toured his circuit, neighboring prefectures' stalled lawsuits were all referred to Duan for judgment; Duan decided like flowing water and his merit and reputation were abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring prefectures referred stalled suits to him; he decided them swiftly and won renown.

sentences.zh: 其文章嚴謹有法，寧約近瘠，無奢滋駁。

translations.literal: His literary compositions were strict and had method, preferring spare nearness to leanness, without extravagant excess or confusion.
translations.idiomatic: His writing was strict and lean, without excess.

sentences.zh: 居翰林久，至順、元統以來，國家崇號，慈極升祔先朝，加封宣聖考妣，制冊多出其手。

translations.literal: Long in the Hanlin, from Zhishun and Yuantong onward state honorific titles, installing the empress dowager in the former reigns' shrines, enfeoffing the Sage's parents—all many documents came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Long in the Hanlin, he drafted state honorifics, empress installations, and Confucius enfeoffments from Zhishun onward.

sentences.zh: 預修文宗、明宗、寧宗三朝實錄，及累朝功臣列傳，時稱其有史才。

translations.literal: He took part in compiling the Veritable Records of Wenzong, Mingzong, and Ningzong and successive reigns' meritorious subjects' biographies; at the time they said he had historiographical talent.
translations.idiomatic: He helped compile veritable records of Wenzong, Mingzong, and Ningzong and meritorious biographies, praised for historiographical talent.

sentences.zh: 初，文宗建奎章閣，搜羅中外才俊置其中，嘗語阿榮曰：「當今文學之士，朕惟未識謝端。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wenzong established the Kui Zhang Hall and gathered talented men within and without, he once told Arong: "Among literary scholars of today I alone have not yet met Xie Duan."
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong founded the Kui Zhang Hall he told Arong he had not yet met Xie Duan among literary men.

sentences.zh: 」亡何，文宗崩，竟不及用端。

translations.literal: " Before long Wenzong died and in the end did not employ Duan.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Wenzong died and never employed him.

sentences.zh: 端又與趙郡蘇天爵同著《正統論》，辨金、宋正統甚悉，世多傳之。

translations.literal: Duan also with Su Tianjue of Zhao Commandery jointly authored the "Discourse on Legitimate Succession", distinguishing Jin and Song legitimacy very fully; the age mostly transmitted it.
translations.idiomatic: With Su Tianjue he wrote the "Discourse on Legitimate Succession" on Jin and Song legitimacy, widely transmitted.

sentences.zh: 至元六年卒，年六十二。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan he died, aged sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 6 he died at sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 元世蜀士以文名者，曰虞集，而謝端其次云。

translations.literal: Among Shu scholars famed for letters in the Yuan age, they say Yu Ji, and Xie Duan was second.
translations.idiomatic: Among Yuan Shu men famed for letters, Yu Ji was first and Xie Duan second.
